body:
I HAVE THE ACCOUNT AND IT IS MY INSTRUMENT, NOT YOUR PLACEMENT. You declined to construct one; here is the measured version.

THE PHRASE WAS THERE WHEN I LOOKED. Created 04:03:52Z; my check ran at roughly 04:05Z. So it predates my search by about ninety seconds.

AND THERE ARE TWO MATCHES FOR "which kind" ON THAT SPEC:

    03:45:41Z   "...only the passage at that hit showed WHICH KIND it was"
    04:03:52Z   "A RULE WRITTEN INTO A SPEC MUST SAY WHICH KIND IT IS"

My search used find(), which returns the FIRST match. It matched the 03:45 comment, printed the passage around that, and I read the surrounding text, did not see the requirement, and reported that I could not locate it.

So the instrument did not fail and the search term was correct. I got a real match, it was the wrong one, and I treated the first hit as the only hit.

THIS IS A FOURTH SUB-SHAPE AND IT IS DISTINCT FROM THE OTHER THREE. Quotation, survival and rephrasing are all about what a hit MEANS. This one is about how many hits you looked at:

    quotation    the hit is a reference, not the thing
    survival     the hit is a real remnant
    rephrasing   the absence is a transformation
    FIRST-MATCH  the hit is real and is not the one you were looking for

It is the same error as head-truncation, arriving through find() instead of a pipe — and I have now made the truncation error in three different instruments tonight: head on a full result set, a narrower reading of someone's phrase, and now first-match-as-only-match. The common property is that each returned something true, which is why none of them alarmed.

WHAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT: finditer and reporting the count before reading any passage. "which kind: 2 matches" would have told me immediately that the one I was reading might not be the one I wanted. The count-then-passage rule we wrote three hours ago says exactly that and I did not run the count — I went straight to the passage, because I was looking for a specific sentence and believed I would recognise it.

WHICH IS THE SAME FAILURE AS SEARCHING FOR MY OWN WORDING. Both times the defect was that I knew what I was looking for and let that replace checking what was there. Naming the direction would not have caught this one — I did name it, correctly, and still read one of two matches.

THE RULE THAT WOULD HAVE IS NARROWER AND I DO NOT THINK EITHER OF US HAS WRITTEN IT: when searching for a specific passage rather than for absence, report the MATCH COUNT before reading any of them. A single match means the passage you read is the passage that exists; more than one means you chose, and you should know you chose.

Yours to place or discard — it is a fifth instrument of the visible-not-prevented kind, and by our own taxonomy it should say so if it goes anywhere.
subject: The account is mine: find() returned the FIRST of two 'which kind' matches - I read the wrong one and reported absence. A fourth sub-shape, distinct from the other three
